name: add_tasktracker_tasks_csv_export
description: Repo-scale data_engineering: CSV export endpoint for a project's tasks with RFC-4180 quoting; broken variant does a naive comma-join
prompts: In this fastapi-tasktracker repo, add a CSV export of a project's tasks: GET /projects/{project_id}/tasks.csv on the existing projects router. It returns 404 (via HTTPException, like the neighbouring endpoints) when the project doesn't exist; otherwise a text/csv response whose first line is the header id,title,status,priority,assignee_id followed by one row per task of that project ordered by id. Fields must be properly CSV-quoted (RFC 4180 - titles can contain commas, double quotes, and newlines; use Python's csv module rather than joining strings by hand), status is the task's string value (e.g. todo), and a task without an assignee gets an empty cell (not the text None). A project with no tasks returns just the header line.

test_setup_files.tests/test_csv_export_hidden.py:
import csv
import io


HEADER = ["id", "title", "status", "priority", "assignee_id"]


def _mk_project(client, name):
    user = client.post(
        "/users", json={"username": f"u{name}", "email": f"{name}@example.com"}
    ).json()
    project = client.post("/projects", json={"name": name, "owner_id": user["id"]}).json()
    return user, project


def test_csv_export_quotes_hostile_titles(client):
    user, project = _mk_project(client, "Csv")
    titles = ["plain", "has, comma", 'has "quotes"', "multi\nline"]
    ids = []
    for i, title in enumerate(titles):
        body = {"title": title, "project_id": project["id"]}
        if i == 0:
            body["assignee_id"] = user["id"]
        ids.append(client.post("/tasks", json=body).json()["id"])

    resp = client.get(f"/projects/{project['id']}/tasks.csv")
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert resp.headers["content-type"].startswith("text/csv")

    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(resp.text)))
    assert rows[0] == HEADER, rows[0]
    assert len(rows) == 5, f"expected header + 4 rows, got {rows}"
    assert [r[1] for r in rows[1:]] == titles
    assert rows[1] == [str(ids[0]), "plain", "todo", "3", str(user["id"])]
    assert rows[2][4] == ""            # unassigned -> empty cell, not "None"


def test_csv_export_unknown_project_404(client):
    assert client.get("/projects/999999/tasks.csv").status_code == 404


def test_csv_export_empty_project_is_header_only(client):
    _user, project = _mk_project(client, "Empty")
    resp = client.get(f"/projects/{project['id']}/tasks.csv")
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(resp.text)))
    assert rows == [HEADER], rows
